# Statute registry worksheet — the 23 open gaps

**Date:** Sep 13, 2026 · **Status:** draft — this is a task list for a human, not a decision
**Implements:** `Build-Plan-Items1-4-Sep2026.md` phase A2
**Generated by:** `src/lib/statuteAudit.ts`, scanning 255 files under `waypoint-app/src/`

---

## Why this exists, and why an agent cannot finish it

`contentSources.ts` says what `verifiedOn` means, and it is unambiguous:

> `verifiedOn` is the date a human confirmed the source says what we say it says.
> Bump it when re-verified; never backdate.

**No agent can honestly stamp that field.** Writing today's date beside a claim
I have not had a human check would be the exact failure this whole workstream
exists to prevent — a citation that looks verified and is not. So this document
goes as far as a machine legitimately can and stops:

- it names every statute asserted in prose with nothing behind it;
- it quotes **what the app actually says**, so the claim can be checked against
  the source rather than guessed at;
- it proposes a canonical URL, marked **UNVERIFIED** in every case;
- it leaves the `claim` line and the `verifiedOn` date to you.

## Why these are not cosmetic

Read the excerpts. Several of these statutes are not decoration in an article —
they sit inside **letter templates a parent sends to a school district or a
Regional Center**, under the heading `Violations:`. A wrong section number there
is a false legal claim made by a family, on Waypoint's word, to an agency that
holds power over their child.

## How to work it

For each entry below, do one of three things:

1. **Register it** — add a `ContentSource` to `src/data/contentSources.ts` with
   the title, the URL you actually opened, the claim in one line, and today's
   date as `verifiedOn`.
2. **Fix the prose** — for anything marked *unattributed*, the statute is
   probably right and only the code name is missing (`§4731` → `W&I §4731`).
   That is a copy change, and it still counts as family-facing.
3. **Remove the claim** — if the section does not say what the app says it
   says, the prose is wrong and the citation should come out, not be registered.

Then delete that entry's line from `KNOWN_GAPS` in
`src/lib/statuteAudit.guard.test.ts`. The ratchet test will confirm it is
genuinely gone — it fails on stale entries as well as new ones, so the list
cannot drift in either direction.

**Do not add to `KNOWN_GAPS` to make a build pass.** A new line there means a
new uncited legal claim shipped to a parent.
